svg.text: Self-learning — six loops, and the adversary each one has to survive
Naive self-learning makes the benchmark problem worse, faster: it is tuning-on-the-test with a cron schedule. The invariant below is what stops that, and every row instantiates it.
Marked on the face: what is shippable inside the freeze, what is roadmap, and the one loop that has already been exercised by hand.

g.text: The invariant, verbatim: no memory updates itself without a named adversary, a held-out gate, an anti-gaming validator, and an append-only promotion record that can be reversed with one write.
1 · A CHANGE IS PROPOSED
column 2 — a constant, a learner model, an item
or a prompt. Never by the loop itself, and
never silently.
2 · A NAMED ADVERSARY ATTACKS IT
column 4 — never the person who built it, and
with an objective function that rewards
breaking the thing under test.
3 · A HELD-OUT GATE DECIDES
column 5 — declared before the run, not after.
Seeds that helped choose a value may never
be the seeds that score it.
4 · AN ANTI-GAMING VALIDATOR
column 6 — it catches the degenerate optimum
an unconstrained sweep finds first, such as a
gate that never fires at all.
5 · AN APPEND-ONLY RECORD
column 3 — config_hash, provenance, and the
sweep that promoted it, with rollback_of so
one write reverses the whole thing.
…and when it goes wrong, that same record un-does it with one write. This is the whole difference between learning and drifting.
THE LOOP
WHAT IT LEARNS
THE MEMORY IT UPDATES
WHO CHALLENGES IT
THE PROMOTION GATE
THE ANTI-GAMING GUARD
L0 · CONSTANTS BECOME DATA
the enabling refactor — nothing else on
this page is buildable until it exists,
and it is three hours of work
FREEZE
27 free constants sit as module-level
literals across six files, against a
benchmark with 17 planted interrupts:
more knobs than there are events.
Nothing on its own. It is the
precondition: tunable literals become
one frozen PolicyConstants model,
injected through Services, with
config_hash = sha256(canonical_json).
Constants become versioned, hashed,
auditable data.
POLICY#core / V#n plus an ACTIVE
pointer. Every Escalation, GradeResult
and item-retirement decision carries
the hash of the constants that made it.
That closes the audit chain from a
parent's question to a specific sweep.
A latent coupling bug, found in the same pass:
adaptation_policy.build_signals passes the same
min_samples to struggle_trigger and to
fast_guess_flag, so sweeping the escalation
threshold silently moved the fast-guessing
detector. Two unrelated thresholds welded
together make any calibration result
uninterpretable. Decouple before sweeping.
Not a gate — the precondition for every gate
below it. Until constants are hashed, no
promotion record can name what it promoted,
and “why were we interrupted?” has no
deterministic answer — only a plausible one,
which is the thing this project refuses.
The code stays byte-stable. The
algorithms a parent's lawyer would
read never change; what changes is a
row with a provenance trail. That is
the whole trick — the deterministic
algorithms never learn their maths,
only their constants.
L1 · REPLAY CALIBRATOR
counterfactual threshold calibration by
deterministic replay — and there is no
LLM anywhere inside this loop
FREEZE
ALREADY EXERCISED
Already exercised by hand: the 8 → 9 move
was chosen on a 2-D slab of disjoint
seeds and scored on 40 virgin ones —
by exactly this loop, driven manually.
escalation_min_samples, cooldown
days, silent days, min active days,
the cohort k-floor, the 0.85 grader
confidence gate, the item-retirement
minimum and the mastery ceilings.
Never the algorithms — only their
constants.
A ConfigVersion row: POLICY#core /
V#n, plus an ACTIVE pointer. “Why were
we interrupted?” then resolves to a
trigger vector, plus the exact
constants in force, plus the sweep
that promoted them — deterministically,
every time, for any escalation.
Adversarial cohort search inside a plausibility
box — an optimiser whose objective is to make
the triggers spam or sleep — plus held-out seed
families, plus a red team behind an information
barrier: given the README and the public API
only, never the trigger code, never the
constants. Publish the worst cohort found,
not the designed one.
Dominance on the held-out seed family (recall ≥,
false alarms ≤, delay ≤), with a paired-bootstrap
95 % CI on each delta excluding zero. Non-inferior
on the adversarial suite. And plateau interiority:
the ±1 neighbours must pass too. A parameter that
works at exactly 8 and fails at 7 and 9 is fitted
noise, not a threshold.
A hard recall floor. A gate that
never fires trivially achieves zero
false alarms, and an unconstrained
sweep finds that degenerate optimum
first. Integer-only candidates a
human can say out loud. Test-seed
hash published; those seeds are run
once per release.
L2 · MASTERY DUEL
EMA against a BKT-style challenger,
shadow-scored on next-response
prediction — harness now, model later
FREEZE
ROADMAP
Why it matters: the 11 residual false
positives are an EMA cold-start artifact
— three consecutive misses multiply the
EMA by 0.7³, from any prior history.
Which learner model predicts the next
response better, per student. And the
deeper move: replacing attempts ≥ 9
with P(mastery < θ) > q, so a hand-
tuned count becomes a stated risk
tolerance that adjusts itself with the
quality of the evidence.
STUDENT#id / MASTERY_MODEL#active —
a pointer plus rolling scores — and a
daily prediction log in S3.
Deliberately not AgentCore Memory:
that tier is conversational, and
putting scoring data in it would
destroy the auditability split.
Each other — and a null baseline that both must
beat: the per-student base rate. If the BKT
challenger cannot beat a per-student base rate
it is ornament, and the report will say so.
Scored on Brier, log-loss, ECE over 10
reliability bins, and AUC. The scoring harness
is worth more than BKT itself: it makes every
future modelling claim in this repo falsifiable.
Rolling Brier improvement ≥ δ over the last
W ≥ 30 responses, sustained for H consecutive
daily evaluations. Demotion at a wider margin —
asymmetric hysteresis, so a student cannot flap
between mastery models mid-week. The model and
its level-calibration map promote as one atomic
pair: a BKT posterior cannot be fed into
ceilings that were tuned for an EMA.
A strict feature cut-off at delivery
time: p(correct) is persisted with a
predicted_at that precedes
received_at, or the row is leakage
and not a label. A leakage detector
on top of it. And the challenger may
not raise interrupt burden at a
fixed recall.
L3 · ITEM COEVOLUTION
generator ↔ critic ↔ probe, with
deterministic psychometrics as the
referee that actually decides
FREEZE
ROADMAP
The referee had to be fixed before it
could referee: the tournament once
retired 20 of 84 items in 14 days on
n ≈ 8 statistics, reported as a feature.
Which items measure anything, and
which generation prompts produce
measurable items. Retirement stops
being a boolean and becomes a typed
reason — too easy, too hard, non-
discriminating, ambiguous, blind-pass
— which flows back into the generator
prompt as an explicit constraint.
ITEM#id / STATS#window, a retirement
ledger, and a regeneration queue.
Provenance.prompt_version already
exists, so every regenerated item is
attributable to the prompt that made
it — which is what lets L4 be scored
on downstream psychometrics rather
than on rubric opinions.
The Answerability Probe, run as an ensemble that
records a blind-pass rate rather than a single
boolean: can a student answer this without ever
seeing the material? Plus its mirror, the
Misconception Probe — a simulated student who
holds the known misconception must get the item
wrong, or the distractors cannot detect the very
error the item was written to detect.
Two-strikes retirement across independent windows:
flag on the point estimate, retire only on
confirmation in a later, separate window. Wilson
intervals, never point estimates. Corrected
item-total correlation, excluding the item from
the total. Discrimination gated at n ≥ 25 — at
pilot scale it is not measurable, and the README
has to say so plainly.
The generator is blinded to the
retired item's response distribution.
A golden set that is immune to
retirement, so the bank cannot drift
out from under the measurement. And
a weekly retirement budget cap — at
most 5 % of the active bank — as a
circuit breaker against collapse.
L4 · PROMPT TOURNAMENTS
prompt-variant tournaments fed by the
human labels the pilot already
generates, for free
FREEZE
ROADMAP
The 0.85 confidence gate is still
unmeasured — offline it is a scripted
constant. Grader-confidence ECE against
human labels is what would back it.
The grader, item-generator and
escalation-composer prompts. Scored
on QWK and MAE over the 0–2 ordinal
rubric points, with cost-asymmetric
rates: a false credit is worse than a
false quarantine, and the metric has
to know that.
PROMPT#agent / V#n plus an ACTIVE
pointer. The calibration corpus lives
in S3 with Object Lock on the test and
golden partitions — a real control
rather than a gesture, since a
tournament that can rewrite its own
test set proves nothing at all.
Human ground truth, already flowing and free:
every quarantine a parent approves, edits or
rejects is a label on the grader, persisted with
the machine's own prediction beside it. Plus a
teacher-labelled golden set of about 60
stratified responses, easy ones included, with
rater_role recorded and teacher labels weighted
above parent labels.
Paired-bootstrap improvement on the held-out
split, and non-regression per stratum.
Quarantine labels are by construction exactly
the low-confidence cases, so a grader prompt
tuned only on them regresses on the confident
majority; promotion requires non-regression on
both strata. Human sign-off on any child-facing
text, without exception.
Variance collapse, constant outputs,
and n-gram overlap between a
candidate prompt and the calibration
items. A quarantine-rate band: 40 %
quarantined is useless even if it is
accurate. And blind audit sampling on
10 % — the proposed grade is hidden,
because parents are approval-biased.
L5 · THE LABEL FLYWHEEL
the exact tuples to persist now — the
substrate every other loop above
has to learn from
FREEZE
BUILD THIS FIRST
The only irreversible item on the list.
Every other loop can be built after the
pilot; signal not captured during it is
gone forever.
Nothing, on its own. Six append-only
record types — Prediction, Outcome,
HumanLabel, Interrupt, ItemStat and
ConfigVersion — plus the one everyone
forgets: NearMiss, every (student, day)
where a trigger almost fired, with the
margin it missed by.
S3 is the corpus of record: daily
JSONL partitions, Athena-queryable,
immutable, Object Lock on the test and
golden partitions. DynamoDB holds only
what needs a point lookup. Local mode
writes the same shapes to disk, with
no credentials at all.
The absence of negatives. Logging only the fires
is the classic flywheel-killer: without near-
misses you can never estimate precision or recall
on real pilot data, and the pilot is the only
external check this project admits to having.
Logging them turns the pilot from an anecdote
generator into a labelled dataset.
Not a gate so much as an invariant: predicted_at
must precede received_at, or the row is leakage
rather than a label. And every InterruptRecord
carries followup_delta — the student's mastery
change on that competency over the next 14 days,
against matched non-interrupted peers. It is the
only path to answering “does interrupting help?”,
and it costs nothing to collect.
Hash, never raw child text. The
learning corpus must not become the
place where the child-data guarantee
leaks, and a text_hash plus a length
is enough for every metric named in
the five columns to the left.
The constraint all of it has to preserve — the deterministic harness stays the referee
Agents choose actions; only auditable deterministic estimators are allowed to cross a threshold. The deterministic algorithms never learn their maths — they learn their constants,
and a constant becomes a versioned, hashed row with a provenance trail that one write reverts. Note the shape: the two loops that touch a child's decisions, L1 and L2, contain no LLM at all.

svg.text: Source: adversarial ML-research review, 2026-08-20. NEAR-TERM = shippable in the current cycle · ROADMAP = later design work, drawn here so the claim stays bounded rather than implied.

Explicitly not being built before the pilot: a generic experimentation platform, any online or continuous learning during a live 30-family pilot, and per-student prompt personalisation. Offline RL and contextual bandits are premature at ~4k–12k decision points — but the propensities are logged anyway, so a later evaluation stays possible.
